title: Basic Geometry
tagline: Year 2 — Lines, angles, triangles, polygons and circles

introduction.overview: Geometry studies shapes, sizes and angles. For aptitude tests the most useful ideas are the angle facts for straight lines and parallel lines, the angle sum of triangles and polygons, the Pythagoras theorem, and a few circle facts. Most questions are one or two steps once you recall the right fact.
introduction.placementRelevance: Basic geometry questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds as angle chasing, polygon facts and right-triangle problems.
introduction.realWorldContext: Construction layouts, screen sizes, road junctions and design drawings all use these facts.

learningObjectives: Use angle relations for straight lines and parallel lines
Apply the angle sum of a triangle and polygon
Use the exterior angle theorem and the triangle inequality
Apply the Pythagoras theorem and common triples

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A straight angle is 180° and a full turn is 360°. Complementary angles add to 90° and supplementary angles to 180°.

coreDefinitions: Complementary angles sum to 90°; supplementary angles sum to 180°.
Triangle: angle sum 180°; the exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
Polygon with n sides: interior angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°; each exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360°/n; number of diagonals = n(n − 3)/2.
Pythagoras: in a right triangle, hypotenuse² = base² + height².
Circle: angle in a semicircle = 90°; the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Geometry facts are conservation laws. Angles along a line always add to 180°, angles round a point to 360°, and angles in a triangle to 180°. Once you find a single missing angle, the rest follow.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Mark everything you know on a quick sketch. Look for straight lines, parallel lines, triangles and circles, and write the corresponding angle fact.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Triangle
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Sum of angles = 180°;  Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Parallel lines
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add to 180°

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Polygons
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Interior sum = (n − 2) × 180°;  Exterior of regular = 360°/n;  Diagonals = n(n − 3)/2
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: n is the number of sides.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Circle
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Angle in a semicircle = 90°;  Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference

mainNarrative: The triangle angle sum is the workhorse: if two angles are 50° and 60°, the third is 70°. The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so an exterior angle of 120° with one opposite angle 50° gives the other as 70°.

Parallel lines cut by a transversal give pairs of equal angles (corresponding and alternate) and pairs adding to 180° (co-interior). If one angle is 65°, the equal one is 65° and the co-interior one is 115°.

For polygons, the interior angle sum is (n − 2) × 180°. A hexagon (n = 6) has 720°, so each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. A regular polygon with exterior angle 36° has 360/36 = 10 sides. The number of diagonals of a hexagon is 6 × 3/2 = 9.
The Pythagoras theorem handles right triangles. Learn the triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 7-24-25. A rectangle with sides 6 and 8 has diagonal 10.

For circles, the angle in a semicircle is 90°, and the angle subtended at the centre by an arc is twice the angle at the circumference. A 100° angle at the centre means 50° at the circumference. Triangle inequality: each side is less than the sum and more than the difference of the other two.

deepDiveAspects.title: Isosceles triangles
deepDiveAspects.content: Equal sides have equal opposite angles. If the apex angle is 40°, each base angle is (180 − 40)/2 = 70°.

deepDiveAspects.title: Triangle inequality
deepDiveAspects.content: With sides 7 and 10, the third side must be between 3 and 17. A value of 18 is impossible.

solvedExamples.title: Exterior angle
solvedExamples.question: An exterior angle of a triangle is 120° and one of the opposite interior angles is 50°. Find the other opposite interior angle.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles.

solvedExamples.title: Regular polygon
solvedExamples.question: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 36°. Find the number of sides and the sum of its interior angles.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Using interior angle sum for exterior angles.

solvedExamples.title: Circle angle
solvedExamples.question: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is 100°. Find the angle subtended by the same arc at a point on the remaining part of the circle.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Angle at the centre is twice that at the circumference.

steps.title: Recall the rule
steps.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The centre angle is twice the circumference angle for the same arc.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Recall the fact that matches the figure (180° line, 180° triangle, (n−2)×180°, 360°/n) and compute in one line.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Mixing which angle is at the centre.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Angles in a triangle must be positive and sum to 180°.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Sketch the figure even if given.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Geometry facts also appear inside mensuration problems.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I find the interior angle of a regular hexagon?
Can I use the exterior angle theorem?
